name: DOE SBIR (incl. FY26 AI topical area)
description: DOE Small Business Innovation Research grants; the FY26 AI topical area is the most concrete near-term federal lane for AI-for-science tooling (precedents: Coreform IGA, RadiaSoft MOOSE-GUI). Phase I ~$200K, Phase II ~$1.1M+.
eligibility: US small business, majority US-owned; PI primarily employed by the firm

name: DOE STTR
description: DOE Small Business Technology Transfer; like SBIR but requires a formal research-institution partner (e.g., a national lab or university).
eligibility: US small business partnered with a US research institution

name: INFUSE (Innovation Network for Fusion Energy)
description: Public-private partnership vouchers pairing private fusion companies with national-lab expertise. IMPORTANT: funds the LAB's work on your behalf — not the company directly (operational leverage, not revenue).
eligibility: Private fusion companies; work performed at DOE labs/universities

name: Milestone-Based Fusion Development Program
description: Cost-shared, pay-for-milestones public-private program modeled on NASA COTS; supports private fusion pilot-plant development.
eligibility: US fusion developers; cost share required

name: FIRE Collaboratives
description: Fusion Innovative Research Engine collaboratives — virtual, multi-institution teams bridging FES science programs and the fusion industry.

name: SciDAC (Scientific Discovery through Advanced Computing)
description: Partnership program funding computational science teams (incl. fusion via SciDAC/FREDA) that pair domain scientists with applied mathematicians and computer scientists.
eligibility: Universities and national labs; industry via partnership

name: INCITE leadership computing allocations
description: Compute allocations (not cash) on DOE leadership systems (Frontier, Aurora); relevant as in-kind support for large-scale simulation campaigns.
eligibility: Open to industry, academia, labs; merit-reviewed

name: ARPA-E OPEN + targeted programs
description: High-risk energy R&D cooperative agreements; periodic OPEN solicitations plus targeted fusion-relevant programs.
eligibility: US entities incl. startups; cost share typically 20%

name: Predictive Science Academic Alliance Program (PSAAP)
description: NNSA-funded university centers for predictive simulation science and V&V/UQ at scale.
eligibility: US universities (centers); industry engagement via partnership

name: Nuclear Energy University Program (NEUP)
description: DOE-NE university R&D and infrastructure grants for advanced fission.

name: GAIN nuclear energy vouchers
description: Gateway for Accelerated Innovation in Nuclear vouchers. Funds national-lab work on behalf of the company (like INFUSE, for fission).
eligibility: US nuclear innovators; work performed at DOE labs

name: NRIC Virtual Test Bed
description: National Reactor Innovation Center virtual test bed for advanced-reactor demonstration modeling (~$2M/yr scale per KB evidence).

name: NSF SBIR/STTR (America's Seed Fund)
description: Equity-free deep-tech seed funding; Phase I ~$305K, Phase II up to ~$1.25M.

name: NIH SBIR/STTR
description: Biomedical SBIR/STTR — largest civilian program; relevant for computational-bio adjacencies.

name: NASA SBIR/STTR
description: Aerospace SBIR/STTR incl. power, propulsion, and simulation tooling topics.

name: DoD SBIR/STTR
description: Defense SBIR/STTR across service branches (AFWERX, Navy, DARPA); dual-use deep tech.
